title: ready-03b: save and restore sessions as JSON
summary: The server writes each session's layout and panes to JSON and rebuilds them on start.
description:
F012 accepted decision "Sessions: palette # mode, CLI flags, … saved as JSON". Depends on P100 (sessions).

## Current state
- Nothing about layout is saved today; the layout types (`heca-core/src/layout/session.rs`, `workspace.rs`, `column.rs`) cannot be written to a file.
- The pattern to reuse: `heca/src/search_state.rs` (T386) — JSON in `dirs::data_dir()/heca/`, a `version` field, atomic write (temp file + rename), `load` never fails (missing / corrupt / future version → empty), saves by itself when a revision counter moves (`persist_if_changed`). Use it, don't write a second one.

## Goal
- Per session: name, project folder, workspaces, columns, panes (sizes as shares), each pane's program and folder, names, focus.
- Saved when something changes (revision), and on exit.
- On server start: rebuild sessions, restart shells in their folders. Running programs cannot be frozen; a hook lets heca-pro resume agents by id.
- A setting to turn it off; a bad file never stops the server.

## Done when
- Quit the server with two sessions of several workspaces and panes; start it again: both sessions come back with the same layout and folders.

tasks.description: Execution task for P105 — read the phase first. Reuse `heca/src/search_state.rs` (T386): data_dir, `version`, atomic write, `load` never fails, save when a revision counter moves. Make the layout types writable (heca-core/src/layout/session.rs, workspace.rs, column.rs) without pulling UI into heca-core. Edge cases: a pane whose folder no longer exists (restart in home, tell the user); a future file version (ignore, keep running); two sessions with the same name; a restore hook for heca-pro to resume agents by id.
